problem: A team needs a project tool quickly, but early adoption can create migration cost before actual workflow needs are known.
goal: Obtain real usage evidence without committing project data to an irreversible structure.
ifr: The team learns which tool fits by using existing representative work while all project data remains exportable and the trial can be stopped without migration loss.
invariants: The trial does not require a long-term paid commitment

claims.statement: The candidate tools support data export in documented formats.
claims.source: frozen vendor export documentation reviewed for the trial

claims.statement: A representative two-week task set will expose the main workflow differences.

contradictions.requirement_a: must begin quickly to generate usage evidence
contradictions.requirement_b: must avoid commitment before evidence exists

solutions.mechanism: Run the same representative tasks in two isolated trial workspaces and score predefined outcomes.
Keep the source data in a neutral format and synchronize only the fields required for the pilot.
risks: The adapter may hide tool-specific limitations

verification: Export and re-import trial data before selection
Measure task completion time and missing workflow capabilities
Stop the trial if an invariant is violated
recommended_next_step: Freeze a representative task set and verify export round-trips before entering live project data.
open_questions: Which workflows are frequent enough to determine selection?
